rationale: Neither candidate surfaces the ground truth's core findings (slot-leak on abort, cumulative/delta re-slice bug, ceil-division length bug, legacy-checkpoint v2-tokenizer ambiguity, missing vendored-header, stale docstrings, WER-fallback raw-bytes skew), so recall is low and roughly tied. X spends much of its review asserting things are 'validated'/'handled' (e.g. claiming the vendored files already carry proper provenance headers), which directly contradicts a ground-truth reviewer's still-open comment and undermines trust in its other unverifiable claims. Y produces more, and more concrete, findings with exact anchors and suggested diffs, most of which are plausible and independently corroborated by X on two items (max_new_frames subscript, dead codes['ref'] extraction), giving it better precision and materially better actionability despite one contested finding (emitted_any/put_req_chunk) that X explicitly argues against.
